regions.full_page: I hope you are well and that the dear Lord guide you. I've "kind-a" been expecting to see you these days and been wanting to write. . . . so our sending a card at least on "Little Christmas,". April 24th, 1949. God help us; it just struck 11 P. M. and want to get this off first in the morning. I just came across this letter of yours of Dec. 18th, 1948. . . . with Mrs. Stanton's $20.00 cheque, etc. I hoped to see you last January and get informed --- instructed rather, etc. What shall I do? I am not clear about anything regarding this matter and it must look to poor Mrs. Stanton as if Fr. Solanus "don't care." I'd like to go into details but. . . . .? I suppose it would be rather out of the question that you could come down closer to St. Felix together. ? We have a "Guests' Apartment," where we could talk things over. We have a "Guest quarters here" to accomodate seven and I am sure you would both enjoy a little visit. am confident that Mr. Stanton was a Christian at heart and a Catholic. I feel too that Mrs. Stanton is at heart a Catholic: for as I have been stressing for years there can be but one Christianity and but one religion - - - the greatest science of all ages and the perfection of that science. God best you both . , all. . .
